statHelp.open: The price of one share when the stock market opened this morning.
statHelp.prevClose: The price of one share when the market closed yesterday.
statHelp.previousClose: The price of one share when the market closed yesterday.
statHelp.daysRange: The lowest and highest price the stock has traded at so far today.
statHelp.week52Range: The lowest and highest price this stock hit over the past year.
statHelp.volume: How many shares were bought and sold today. Bigger means more people are trading it.
statHelp.avgVolume3m: The average number of shares traded each day over the last 3 months.
statHelp.marketCap: The total value of the whole company: share price times the number of shares that exist.
statHelp.mktCap: The total value of the whole company: share price times the number of shares that exist.
statHelp.netAssets: The total value of everything this fund holds.
statHelp.sharesOutstanding: The total number of shares the company has created.
statHelp.peTtm: Price-to-Earnings: how much investors pay for each $1 the company earns. Higher = pricier.
statHelp.forwardPe: Like P/E, but based on how much the company is expected to earn next year.
statHelp.priceSales: The company's value compared to how much money it makes in sales.
statHelp.priceBook: The company's value compared to what its assets are worth on paper.
statHelp.epsTtm: Earnings Per Share: the profit the company made for each share over the past year.
statHelp.forwardEps: The profit per share the company is expected to make next year.
statHelp.revenueTtm: All the money the company brought in from sales over the past year.
statHelp.ebitda: A measure of profit before subtracting things like taxes and interest.
statHelp.profitMargin: Out of every $1 the company makes, how much is actual profit.
statHelp.operatingMargin: How much profit the company keeps from its main business, before taxes and interest.
statHelp.beta5yMonthly: How wild the price swings are compared to the whole market. Above 1 means bumpier than average.
statHelp.targetEst1y: What experts guess the price could be one year from now.
statHelp.dividendYield: The yearly cash a company pays you, shown as a % of the share price.
statHelp.dividendRate: The amount of cash a company pays you per share each year.
statHelp.exDividendDate: You need to own the stock before this date to get the next dividend payment.
statHelp.sharesOwned: How many shares of this stock you own right now.
statHelp.avgPurchasePrice: The average price you paid for each share you own.
statHelp.currentValue: What all of your shares are worth right now.
statHelp.profitLoss: How much you've gained or lost since you bought, in coins and percent.

bonds.noCertificatesHint: Buy a bond from the market and your certificates will live here, each with a countdown to payday.
bonds.howBondsWorkBody: a bond is a loan you give to a government or company, and they pay you interest for it. Safer issuers pay less; riskier issuers pay more - but the higher the yield, the bigger the default chance that they can't repay and you lose what you put in. Your money stays locked until it matures.

maya.background: Ran a profitable Etsy shop for two years while in school.
answers: I've run my own small shop, so I know what it takes to keep customers happy and the books balanced - I want to do that at a bigger scale here.
When my supplier flaked right before a holiday rush, I found two backups in a day and still shipped every order on time.
I batch similar tasks, knock out the highest-impact one first, and keep a running list so nothing slips.

priya.background: Treasurer of two school clubs; strong with numbers.
answers: I love the operations side - budgets, scheduling, and making things actually run smoothly.
Our club's budget was a mess; I rebuilt the spreadsheet line by line and we ended the year in surplus.
I prioritize by deadline and impact, and I'm not afraid to ask for help early instead of falling behind.

jordan.background: Worked two summers in retail customer service.
answers: I'm good with customers and reliable, and I want to grow into more responsibility than a register.
A customer was furious about a refund; I stayed calm, listened, and got it sorted within policy.
I make a quick to-do list and ask which thing matters most if I'm unsure.

sam.background: Recent grad, no direct experience but eager.
answers: It seems like a cool opportunity and I could really use a job right now.
Um… I helped a friend move once? I'm pretty reliable I guess.
I just kind of do whatever's in front of me until it's done.

tyler.background: Lists a lot of hobbies, vague on actual work.
answers: Honestly I'm not totally sure - a friend told me to apply.
I can't really think of one right now, sorry.
I usually just wing it and hope it works out.
